The Butlers’ Method FAQs

Still have questions?
‍AHere are the straight answers

How much does a website project cost?

Website projects start at $10,000. Most full-cycle B2B website engagements fall between $25,000 and $50,000.A focused landing page or a smaller corporate website may fall within the $10,000–$20,000 range, especially when the brand, structure, and content are already prepared.

Projects that include research, positioning, copywriting,UX/UI design, development, CMS setup, and integrations typically require a larger investment.

Complex platforms and custom functionality may exceed $50,000. After the first conversation, we will explain what yourproject realistically requires, what can be prioritised,and provide a clear estimate before any work begins.

So, leave us a message, and we’ll provide you with a realistic estimate. If you’d like to learn more about our process, check out our /how-we-work page.

Which platform and technology stack should we use?

We recommend the technology based on your business, content, integrations, internal team, and long-term plans.

We build scalable websites with Webflow, WordPress, Shopify, and HubSpot, as well as custom and headless solutions using React, Vue, Node.js, Laravel, and Strapi.

If your company already has technical requirements, we can work within them. If not, we will explain the trade-offs and recommend the most practical option.

Whatever the stack, the goal remains the same: a fast, accessible, easy-to-manage website that can grow with the company.

Can you move faster if we have a hard deadline?

Yes, when the deadline is realistic and the trade-offs are understood.

We can increase the team, run design and development tasks in parallel, and prioritise the parts required for launch. In some cases, we can also simplify the initial scope and refine less critical elements afterwards.

That is how we launched TorchSensors in time for a major media feature. The product started receiving preorders immediately, while we returned to improve the code and animations after the urgent launch.

Speed should be a conscious business decision, not a reason to hide risks. Before starting, we will explain what can be accelerated, what cannot, and what will need attention after launch.

How are payments structured?

For full-cycle projects (research, design and development), payments are split into three parts: 30% upfront, 40% after design approval, and 30% on completion — before the final transfer.

For smaller, single-scope services — like design only, implementing your mockups in code, or similar — it’s usually 50 / 50: half upfront and half on delivery, before we hand over the source files.

What does your website process look like?

We take responsibility for the complete journey: discovery, research, positioning, website structure, copywriting, UX/UI design, development, integrations, testing, and launch.

The same senior team stays involved throughout the project, so the original business goals do not get lost between strategy, design, and development.

After launch, we remain involved for three months to monitor the website, resolve issues, review real behaviour, and improve the experience around the goals defined at the start.

You can see every stage in detail on our How We Work page.

How many design concepts do you provide?

If you already have an established brand system, we usually create one strong visual direction with up to three variations.

If the visual direction still needs to be defined, we can explore three distinct concepts before developing the selected one further.

We do not simply send several unrelated designs and ask you to choose. Before and during the design stage, we review references together, collect structured feedback, and build a clear list of what should and should not be used.

The goal is not only to create something you like. It is to find a direction that represents the company correctly and works for its audience.

Can you create the website structure and user journeys?

Yes. You do not need to come to us with a finished sitemap or a complete set of wireframes.

We can research your audiences and competitors, review the existing website and analytics, define the information architecture, structure individual pages, write the content, and create wireframes and interactive prototypes.

For complex B2B companies, this is often one of the most important parts of the project. The website needs to make the offer understandable before it can make it attractive.

If your marketing or product team already has research, content, or an approved structure, we will work with those materials instead of repeating the work.

Do you provide website copywriting?

Yes. Copywriting can be included as part of the complete website process.

Our UX and content specialists first define what each page and section needs to communicate: the audience’s questions, objections, priorities, and reasons to trust the company. The copywriter then turns that structure into clear, concise website content.

Because the copy and design are developed together, the message does not have to be forced into layouts created without it.

We can also work with your internal copywriter or marketing team if you prefer to produce the final content in-house.

Do you handle SEO and AI search readiness?

Every website includes a strong technical SEO foundation: metadata, Open Graph tags, XML sitemaps, redirects, alt text, clean code, performance optimisation, and a clear semantic content structure.

Where relevant, we can also implement schema markup and organise the content so that it is easier for search engines and AI-powered discovery tools to understand.

We do not provide ongoing SEO promotion, backlink acquisition, or large-scale keyword campaigns in-house. If those services are required, we can collaborate directly with your SEO team or a specialised partner.

Our role is to make sure the website gives them a technically sound and scalable foundation to work with.

Can you handle analytics, CRM, AI, and other integrations?

Yes. We can connect the website with the tools your marketing, sales, and operations teams already use.

This includes analytics platforms, HubSpot, Pipedrive, Zoho, Mailchimp, GetResponse, Twilio, booking systems, real estate platforms, and other third-party services.

We can also integrate AI-powered search, assistants, content workflows, automation, and other AI functionality where it solves a real user or business problem.

If a service provides an API, we can usually integrate it directly. If its data or documentation is incomplete, we can build a small custom service to organise the connection.

AI where useful. No AI theatre.

What happens during and after post-launch support?

We remain involved for three months after launch.

During the first month, we gather data, monitor behaviour, and establish a reliable baseline. During the second, we resolve issues and test improvements. During the third, we build on what works and prepare further recommendations.

At the end of this period, you receive a clear summary of what was reviewed, what changed, and what we recommend next.

Minor fixes and improvements are included. Larger additions, such as new pages, campaigns, or functionality, are estimated separately.

After the initial three months, we can continue through ongoing optimisation or a 6- or 12-month support agreement.

How quickly do you respond to urgent issues?

We respond as soon as we receive an emergency message and typically begin investigating within one working hour during our normal business hours.

You can reach us through email, Slack, WhatsApp, or Telegram, depending on how the project communication is organised.

We intentionally keep part of the team’s capacity available instead of scheduling every developer at 100%. This allows us to react to urgent production issues without abandoning other active projects.

For critical systems that require guaranteed response times outside normal working hours, we can discuss a dedicated support agreement.
